justification: Single-arm WHO-protocol efficacy study of standard-dose sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in children 6-59 months with uncomplicated falciparum malaria, the labelled setting and regimen. justification: Randomised placebo-controlled trial of metformin pre-treatment and co-administration in infertile PCOS women aged 35-45 with predictors of poor ovarian response, using a flare-up IVF protocol with high-dose FSH. web_findings: The registry lists the publication (Palomba 2011, Fertil Steril, PMID 21917254; abstract read). A sister trial from the same group (NCT01233206, high-responder PCOS, completed) lists a publication titled 'Metformin reduces risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome in patients with PCOS during gonadotropin-stimulated IVF cycles'. 2023 international PCOS guideline: adjunct metformin could be used before/during FSH stimulation in women with PCOS having IVF/ICSI on a GnRH-agonist long protocol to reduce OHSS and miscarriage; metformin for PCOS is off-label. The US metformin label lists only type 2 diabetes.

justification: Randomised phase III in untreated advanced gastric cancer comparing experimental fractionated docetaxel-oxaliplatin-capecitabine (Low-TOX) with the standard EOX regimen, whose epirubicin arm is the control. justification: Single-arm WHO-style efficacy study of single-dose sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Gabon, matching the Fansidar label setting and regimen. This is loss of efficacy to resistance, not toxicity.
web_findings: No results are posted on the registry. The linked publication (Mombo-Ngoma et al., Malar J 2011, PMID 21569596) reports 29 children treated, termination 'on the grounds of unexpected high therapeutic failure rates', PCR-corrected adequate response 12/26 (46%), late parasitological failure 13/26 (50%), early treatment failure 1/26 (4%), 92% dhfr triple-mutant isolates, SP well tolerated, failures rescued with artemether-lumefantrine. The Open Targets safety category rests on the registry wording 'concerns about safety of children', which in the paper means treatment failure rather than drug toxicity. The Fansidar FDA label (NDA 18-557, 2004 revision) indicates treatment of acute, uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in patients in whom chloroquine resistance is suspected, gives weight-based single-dose treatment for children older than 2 months, and warns that SP resistance is prevalent in East and Central Africa. Current US pyrimethamine labels list only toxoplasmosis, and for uncomplicated falciparum malaria the WHO guidelines list SP only as part of artesunate plus SP, so the tested monotherapy is a historical rather than a current guideline regimen and the failure reflects regional resistance; this is why confidence is medium.

justification: LOSS compared an intensive medical programme (liquid diet, group counselling, and sibutramine, orlistat or diethylpropion chosen by the physician) with website-only usual care in BMI 40-60. Label: short-term adjunct in exogenous obesity, BMI 30 or higher.

justification: TARDIS tested 30 days of triple antiplatelet therapy (aspirin, clopidogrel, dipyridamole) against guideline therapy (clopidogrel alone, or aspirin plus dipyridamole) within 48 hours of stroke or TIA. Aspirin label (Durlaza): reduce risk of death and recurrent stroke after ischemic stroke or TIA.

justification: Takeda's postmarketing study compared pioglitazone with glyburide for up to 24 weeks in type 2 diabetes with NYHA class II-III systolic heart failure (LVEF <40%); the DSMB stopped it for more heart-failure events on pioglitazone (primary endpoint 13% vs 8%). justification: Placebo-controlled trial of escitalopram 10 mg daily for major depression in advanced lung or gastrointestinal cancer; 24 of 220 planned patients were randomised. justification: Two phase I dose-finding combinations that include lapatinib as a co-escalated partner: KW-2450 plus lapatinib and letrozole, and lapatinib plus pegylated liposomal doxorubicin. web_findings: The KW-2450 paper (PMID 30083253) contradicts the registry wording: dose-limiting toxicities (grade 3 rash, hyperglycaemia) occurred at KW-2450 25 mg + lapatinib 1500 mg + letrozole, but the recommended phase 2 dose (KW-2450 25 mg, lapatinib 1250 mg, letrozole 2.5 mg) had no DLT, and phase 2 did not start because of anticipated enrolment difficulty and end of KW-2450 development. The lapatinib/PLD paper (PMID 28341957): 11 enrolled, 1 DLT (grade 3 diarrhoea) at level 2, grade 3 events after cycle 1 led to closing level 3; combination called feasible and potentially active. justification: TRIGGER-PCI tested prasugrel against clopidogrel in stable coronary disease patients with high platelet reactivity after elective stenting (recent MI excluded), not the labelled acute coronary syndrome managed with PCI. justification: CHAMPION PCI tested the labelled cangrelor bolus-plus-infusion as PCI adjunct (ACS and stable angina) against 600 mg clopidogrel given just before PCI. Kengreal label: PCI adjunct in P2Y12-naive patients based on CHAMPION PHOENIX; section 14.2 states CHAMPION PCI and PLATFORM were terminated early for futility.

justification: Planned phase 1/2 PrEP study of long-acting injectable rilpivirine (TMC278LA 600 mg intramuscular monthly) in HIV-negative healthy volunteers, a prevention use with a depot formulation, unlike the labelled oral treatment of HIV-1 infection. web_findings: Registry: start 2010-03, closed 2010-05, 0 enrolled, no results; no publication of this trial found and the nature of the additional safety information is not stated. FDA labels: oral Edurant is for treatment of HIV-1 in combination with other antiretrovirals; Cabenuva (cabotegravir plus long-acting rilpivirine) is for treatment in virologically suppressed patients, not PrEP.
